title: Using AI to support education for Collective Intelligence
extended_summary:
This paper asks how artificial intelligence can be used to support education for collective intelligence (CI), understood as thinking together, solving problems together, and making decisions together. The authors argue that prior AI in education work has focused mostly on individual learning, whereas CI requires support for group formation, collaborative dialogue, and orchestration of multi-stage group work.

To address this question, the paper conducts a scoping literature review and thematic analysis of 46 empirical studies published up to April 2023, supplemented by conceptual analysis. The review covers AI-enabled education research across classrooms, MOOCs, citizen science, crowdsourcing, and other collaborative settings. The studies include AI used as embedded analytics in environments and as explicit agents or chatbots.

The authors synthesize the literature into a three-part framework: AI for grouping, AI for process support, and AI for staging. Grouping refers to algorithms that form productive teams or recommend peers; process refers to coaching dialogue and collaborative interaction; staging refers to helping groups progress through phases of a collaborative task. The paper concludes that AI has promise for supporting CI across small groups and large or unbounded communities, but that much of the evidence remains exploratory, context-specific, and focused on feasibility or usability rather than strong causal effects.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI / chatbot tool based on large language models, used conversationally for education and assistance tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses generative AI and LLM-based chatbots as a potential way to support dialogue, coaching, and orchestration in education for collective intelligence, but does not evaluate a specific generative AI product in an empirical study.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a literature review and conceptual framework paper, not a primary evaluation of a specific AI tool. It synthesizes prior studies but does not report original experimental outcomes for a named system.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct effect sizes or outcome data are reported for a specific tool in this paper. The paper is about proposed uses and categories of AI support rather than measured impact.
